hero.headline: Martin County brush fires contained, but Florida Forest Service warns more expected this summer
hero.body:
Martin County saw two brush fires this week, including one sparked by a lightning strike. Both fires are now fully contained and being monitored by the Florida Forest Service. Officials say the conditions that fuel these fires are not going away anytime soon, but residents should not be alarmed.

David Grubitch, a mitigation specialist and spokesperson with the Florida Forest Service, said this is their peak season. The summer heat is drying out fine dead fuels, making them ready to ignite when lightning strikes occur. Grubitch explained that rain often extinguishes these fires immediately, but sometimes they travel underground and surface days later. He emphasized that the intense heat that makes people want to stay indoors is the same heat drying out materials that become fire fuel.

Grubitch said the public plays a crucial role in helping the Florida Forest Service do its job. He stressed that residents should never assume someone else has already called in a brush fire. If you see something, say something, he said, as it can make all the difference in how quickly crews are able to get a fire under control. Quick reporting allows firefighters to respond faster and contain blazes before they spread.

The Florida Forest Service continues to monitor conditions across the region as the summer fire season continues. While officials warn that the weather patterns creating these fire risks will persist, they emphasize there is no need for panic. Residents are encouraged to remain vigilant and report any signs of fire immediately to help crews respond as quickly as possible.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner Beats Alexander Zverev to Win Second Consecutive Wimbledon Title
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner defeated Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday to claim his second consecutive Wimbledon title at the All England Club.
cards.body:
Top-ranked Jannik Sinner defeated Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday to claim his second consecutive Wimbledon title at the All England Club. The Italian's fifth Grand Slam title came in his first tournament since a second-round meltdown at the French Open, when he wilted in a Paris heat wave. When Sinner ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point, he dropped to the grass on his back in celebration.

The match turned at 3-3 in the third set when Zverev earned his first break point after 2 hours and 42 minutes of play. Sinner produced a drop shot and Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline. Zverev grasped his knee in apparent discomfort and Sinner went around the net and helped his opponent up off the grass. Zverev quickly resumed playing but appeared slightly hampered and slung his racket across the baseline in frustration when he missed a forehand and handed Sinner the first break of the match and a 5-3 lead in the third.

A year ago, Sinner beat Carlos Alcaraz in the final at the All England Club after wasting three match points against his rival in the Roland Garros final. It was Sinner's 10th straight victory over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open. Prince William joined his wife Kate and two of their children for the final in a star-studded Royal Box that also included actors Dustin Hoffman, Nicole Kidman and Ben Stiller.

Amid stifling heat and humidity in Paris in late May, Sinner had his 30-match winning streak ended after coming within one game of a straight-set victory over Juan Manuel Cerundolo, who was ranked No. 56. Sinner went in for medical exams in Milan after the Paris defeat and didn't play an official match again until he arrived at Wimbledon, where he twice had to come back from a set down in a five-set marathon against Miomir Kecmanovic in the first round. Despite the defeat in the final, Zverev will leapfrog Alcaraz into the No. 2 spot in the rankings on Monday.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Three-Game Skid With 4-1 Win Over Jupiter
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed o
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets snapped a three-game losing streak Saturday evening with a wire-to-wire 4-1 win over the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie needed only minutes to take control. The first three batters of the game all reached and scored before an out was recorded. Elian Peña opened with a single, Mike Tauchman doubled him home, and Trey Snyder followed with a two-run homer off Walin Castillo for a 3-0 lead.

Julio Zayas added a solo shot with two outs in the third to push the margin to 4-0.

That was more than enough for starter Emilio Obispo, who threw five shutout innings and lowered his season ERA to 1.82. He scattered four singles, walked three and struck out six to earn his fourth win of the year.

Obispo worked out of trouble when it mattered. He struck out Josh Hogue to strand the bases loaded in the third, induced a double play to end the fourth, and retired the side in order in the fifth to finish his outing.

Jupiter loaded the bases against Calvin Ziegler in the sixth. Ziegler struck out Jake McCutheon for the second out before Zack Mack entered and ended the threat with a popout. Mack went 2.1 innings and allowed one unearned run, which came in the eighth when Andres Valor stole third and scored on a throwing error.

Elwis Mijares closed it out with a 1-2-3 ninth on 11 pitches for his second save.

Tauchman, rehabbing a torn meniscus, went 1 for 3 with the double, an RBI and a run while playing six innings in left field in his first rehab game with St. Lucie. Snyder led the offense at 2 for 4 with the homer and two RBI.

The Mets (5-13, 38-46) and Hammerheads (8-12, 45-41) close their six-game series Sunday at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. A win would give St. Lucie its first 3-3 series split of 2026. First pitch is 12:30 p.m.

cards.headline: TCCEED doubles employer participation in second year of paid summer internship program
cards.teaser: TCCEED placed 61 Treasure Coast students in paid summer internships this year, doubling employer participation and tripling student applications from the first year of the program.
cards.body: TCCEED expanded its paid summer internship program in its second year, doubling employer participation and placing 61 students in local jobs. Applications from Treasure Coast students tripled compared to the first year of the initiative. The program connects students with paid work experience at local businesses and organizations across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova Wins Wimbledon Women's Title After Saving Five Match Points
cards.teaser: The 21-year-old Czech player recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. The 21-year-old became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024. Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance.

Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club, looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie soccer stadium groundbreaking set for November, new renderings show 6,000-seat venue
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie SC released new renderings this week of its 6,000-seat soccer stadium planned for the Walton & One development, a 46-acre mixed-use project at U.S. 1 and Walton Road. Groundbreaking is now targeted for November, with the facility scheduled to open in early 2028. The club begins its inaugural season in 2027 at a yet-to-be-announced home venue. The team has not disclosed where it will play next year while construction is underway.

The stadium is an $80 million economic investment, and no taxpayer money will be used for its construction, according to the city. Port St. Lucie City Council members unanimously approved funding and operating agreements in October when the city was awarded a United Soccer League (USL) League One Team. Ticket deposits are currently available online.

Port St. Lucie resident Zach Woods said the stadium could bring the city its first major attraction. Businesses near the site, including Sapps Barbershop, anticipate increased foot traffic. Barber Focus Sanders said the venue will bring more people to the area, including visitors from out of town.

Concerns about traffic on U.S. 1 remain a reservation for some residents. Woods said traffic in the area is already difficult, and gameday crowds will worsen congestion. The club says the venue will host matchdays, concerts, festivals and community events year-round, with the flexibility to expand beyond its 6,000-seat capacity.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie ranks 67th most stressed city in US, financial stress cited as key factor
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie was ranked the 67th most stressed city in the United States and 42nd most financially stressed according to a WalletHub study released this month.
cards.body:
A new study released this month by WalletHub ranked Port St. Lucie as the 67th most stressed city in the United States. The report cited the city as the 42nd most financially stressed in America. The study compared 182 cities across 39 metrics, which included average weekly work hours, unemployment rate, divorce and suicide rates. Jacksonville is the most stressed city in Florida, ranking 37th in the nation.

Florida performed fairly well compared to other states, with no cities in the top 35. In South Florida, Miami was ranked 50th, with affordable housing being fourth worst in the U.S., and Fort Lauderdale at 83rd. Detroit, Baltimore, Cleveland, Memphis and Shreveport, Louisiana topped the list of most stressed cities in the country. Fremont, California, in the Bay Area, a notably affluent area with average home prices of about $1.5 million, topped the list of least stressed cities, followed by South Burlington, Vermont, and Bismarck and Fargo, North Dakota. WalletHub analyst Chip Lupo said cities with high crime rates, weak economies, less effective public health and congested transportation systems naturally lead to elevated stress levels for residents. The report found that money, health and the economy all remain top stressors.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to panoramic views
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, offers visitors a 105-step climb to panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, has guided ships along Florida's Atlantic coast for more than 165 years. The red brick tower rises at the base of the Jupiter Inlet. The 105-step climb to the top takes visitors up a narrow spiral staircase that lighthouse keepers once used as they climbed night after night to keep the powerful Fresnel lens shining for mariners.

From the gallery at the top, panoramic views reveal the Atlantic Ocean stretching to the east. Below, the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet meet the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers. Boats glide through the channel as the sea breeze sweeps across the observation area. The museum grounds feature restored historic buildings that detail the lighthouse's history from its construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station.

hero.headline: Karolina Muchova Ends Coco Gauff's Wimbledon Run in Dramatic Tiebreaker
hero.teaser: Karolina Muchova defeated Coco Gauff 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) on Thursday in a match that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, becoming the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the Wimbledon final.
hero.body:
Karolina Muchova ended Coco Gauff's run at Wimbledon with a 6-2, 1-6, 7-6 (10) victory Thursday that ended with a drama-filled tiebreaker, to become the fourth Czech woman in the last six years to reach the final of the grass-court Grand Slam. It will be the ninth-ranked Muchova's second Grand Slam final after losing to Iga Swiatek in the 2023 French Open championship match. Muchova could face another Czech player in Saturday's final, with Linda Noskova to play Marta Kostyuk of Ukraine in the other semifinal next on Centre Court.

For Gauff, it was still her most successful Wimbledon. Previously, the seventh-ranked American had gone only as far as the fourth round three times, including during her breakthrough run as a 15-year-old in 2019. The other Czech women in the Wimbledon final recently were Karolina Pliskova, who was runner-up in 2021, Marketa Vondrousova, who was champion in 2023, and Barbora Krejcikova, who was champion in 2024. The men's semifinals on Friday feature top-ranked and defending champion Jannik Sinner against seven-time Wimbledon winner Novak Djokovic and French Open champion Alexander Zverev against British wild card Arthur Fery.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie teen to serve as flag bearer at FIFA World Cup finals
hero.teaser: Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club
hero.body:
Enrique Rosario Liz, a Port St. Lucie teenager named Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, was surprised Friday at the Boys & Girls Club of St. Lucie County in Fort Pierce with a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity. He will serve as one of 12 club members from across the country selected to be an official Coca-Cola flag bearer at the FIFA World Cup finals on July 19. The surprise came courtesy of the Boys & Girls Clubs of America and their partnership with the Coca-Cola Company. When the box containing the news was walked into the room surrounded by fellow club members, his reaction was immediate. "I mean, this is so insane," Rosario Liz said. Along with the trip, he also received official gear inside the box.

Rosario Liz had already been juggling a packed summer, preparing for move-in at the University of Florida and an internship, but said the World Cup had been on his mind. "My time is really being taken up by the World Cup right now, forcing my parents to watch every game," Rosario Liz said. He credited the Boys & Girls Club with shaping who he has become as a leader. "The club really helped me to find what my leadership style was going to be, and really redefined what my definition of leadership was," Rosario Liz said. The recognition as a flag bearer comes after his selection as Youth of the Year for the Southeast Region, one of the highest honors given by the Boys & Girls Clubs of America.

As one of only 12 club members chosen nationally for this role, Rosario Liz will represent not only his local club in St. Lucie County but also youth organizations across the country at the World Cup finals. "The Boys & Girls Clubs has been my everything," he said. He closed with a message for younger members at the club. "Please stay with your Boys & Girls Clubs, because one day I want to see each and every one of you in the same position that I am in right now," Rosario Liz said.

The announcement marks a significant milestone for the Port St. Lucie teen as he prepares to transition to college life at the University of Florida while taking on this prestigious international role at the World Cup finals. The opportunity showcases the impact of the Boys & Girls Clubs program on young leaders and highlights the partnership between the youth organization and the Coca-Cola Company in providing exceptional experiences for outstanding club members.
